chunks: He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar reported to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Anbari, from Abu al-Hasan Humaid ibn Muhammad ibn Humaid al-Tamimi, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Nuaim al-Abdi, from Abu Ali al-Ru'asi ibn Abdullah, from Abu Masud Ubaid ibn Sami', from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

When the delegation of Iyad came to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family and progeny, he asked them: 'What happened to Quss ibn Sa'idah?' They said: 'He died, O Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: 'May Allah have mercy on Quss ibn Sa'idah. It is as if I am looking at him in the marketplace of Ukaz, seated on a grey camel, speaking eloquent words upon which there was a sweetness that I cannot recall.'

A man from the delegation said: 'I remember it, O Messenger of Allah. I heard him saying at the marketplace of Ukaz: O people, hear, heed, and remember! Whoever lives shall die, and whoever dies is gone, and all that is coming shall come. A dark night, a sky full of constellations, swelling seas and gleaming stars, rain and vegetation, fathers and mothers, those who go and those who come, light and darkness, good and sin, clothing and finery and mounts, food and drink. Indeed in the heavens there is news, and indeed on the earth there are lessons! Why do I see people going and never returning? Did they settle there contentedly? Or were they left behind and fell asleep? Quss ibn Sa'idah swears by Allah a solemn oath with no sin in it: there is no religion more beloved to Allah on earth than a religion whose time has overshadowed you and whose era has reached you. Blessed is the one who encounters its bearer and follows him, and woe to the one who encounters him and turns away.' Then he recited:

'In the early ones who have departed, from the ages past, there are insights for us. When I saw that death has approaches with no ways of returning, and I saw my people heading toward it — the young and the old — the past does not return to you, nor does any ancient one remain. I became certain that inevitably I shall go where the people have gone.'
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: 'May Allah have mercy on Quss ibn Sa'idah. I hope he will come on the Day of Resurrection as a community unto himself.'

A man from the delegation said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I saw something amazing about Quss.' He asked: 'What did you see?' He said: 'One day I was near a mountain in our region called Sam'an, on an extremely hot summer day, when I came upon Quss ibn Sa'idah in the shade of a tree near a spring of water, and around him were many wild animals that had come to drink from the water. When one animal roared at another, he struck it with his hand and said: Wait until the one who came before you has finished drinking. When I saw him and the wild animals around him, I was terrified and a severe fear entered me. He said to me: You have nothing to worry about, do not fear, God willing. Then I saw two graves with a mosque between them. When I became familiar with him, I asked: What are these two graves? He said: The graves of two brothers of mine who used to worship Allah in this place with me. They died, so I buried them here and built a mosque between them where I worship Allah until I join them.' Then he mentioned their days and their deeds, and he wept, then said:

'O my two friends, arise! You have slept so long. I find you still have not finished your slumber. Do you not know that I am alone at Sam'an, and I have no one there whom I loved besides you two? I stand by your graves, not departing, through all the nights, until I hear your voices. I weep for you all of life long, but what can tears return to one who laments? It is as if you two and death are the nearest goal — by my soul in my grave, just as it came upon you. If a soul could serve as a shield for another soul, I would have offered my own soul to be your ransom.'

key_terms.أمة وحده: A community unto himself — meaning Quss will be resurrected as a singular righteous nation
key_terms.سوق عكاظ: The marketplace of Ukaz, a major pre-Islamic trade fair near Ta'if
key_terms.قس بن ساعدة: Quss ibn Sa'idah al-Iyadi, bishop of the Iyad tribe, a pre-Islamic monotheist known for eloquent oratory

ai.seo_question: Who was Quss ibn Sa'idah and what did the Prophet Muhammad say about him?
ai.summary: This long narrative reports the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) recollection of Quss ibn Sa'idah al-Iyadi, a pre-Islamic monotheist and orator renowned at the Ukaz marketplace. The Prophet fondly remembered his eloquent speech, and a companion recited Quss's famous sermon on the inevitability of death, the signs of God in creation, and his prophecy of a coming religion. A second account describes Quss living as an ascetic in the mountains, commanding wild animals, worshipping at the graves of his two deceased companions and mourning them in moving poetry.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 7. He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar reported to me from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Anbari, who reported from Abul Hasan Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Tameemi, who reported from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Nuaim al-Abdi, who reported from Abu ‘Ali al-Rawwasi ibn Abdullah, who reported from Abu Masood Ubaid ibn Samee’, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Swaleh, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

When the delegation of Ayad called upon the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, he asked them: "What happened to Quss ibn Sa’edah?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah! he died." The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: "May Allah bless Quss ibn Sa’edah with mercy, it is as if I am looking at him in the marketplace of Ukkaz, seated on the grey camel. He spoke very pleasently, which I did not try to remember."

A man from the delegation said: "I have memorized it, O, Prophet of Allah! I heard him say at Ukkaz: "O people! Hear, listen and remember (me). He who lives must die, and he who dies loses the opportunity (for acts). And all that is expected will soon occur. (Ponder upon) the dark night and the heavens full of constellations, and swelling seas and the gleaming stars and the rains and the vegetation and the fathers and the mothers, and those who go and those who come, and the light and the darkness and the good and the evil, and the clothes and attire and that which you ride, eat and drink! Surely, there is a heavenly news in the sky, and no doubt there are lessons to draw from (the events on) the earth. How come I see men go and never return? Is it because they liked the place there, therefore they stayed? Or were they left so they fell asleep? Quss ibn Sae’dah swears by Allah, a solemn oath which has no blemish. There is no religion, which Allah likes more than the one whose duration overwhelms you and which covers your period (in all its aspects). Blessed are those who will find the bringer of that faith and then follow him, and woe unto him who will find him but reject him."

Then he said: "The early ones who have gone away since centuries, in them there are examples for us; When I saw that death has departures, with none to be stopped or returned. And I saw my people going towards it - all, big and small ones. The bygone does not return to you, nor anyone from ancient times, I am certain that quite inevitably, I will be gone, the way the people have gone."
Then the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny said: "Allah may bless Quss ibn Sa’edah with mercy. I hope he will rise on the Day of Resurrection as a single model (of virtue)."

The man from the delegation said: "O Prophet of Allah! I saw something amazing about Quss." He (i.e. the Prophet) asked: "What was that?" He said: One day, as I was standing near a mountain in our district called Sam’aan, on an extremely hot summer day, I saw Quss ibn Sa’edah standing under the shadow of a tree, and there was a stream flowing. Around the stream were several animals that had arrived to drink. There a wild animal jostled another with its paw. Quss hit him with his hands and said: "Wait till the one who has come before you has finished drinking." When I saw him, and the animals around him, I felt frightened. He said: "You do not have to worry. Do not fear, Allah willing." Then I came across two graves with a mosque in between. When I became close to him, I asked about those two graves. He said: "These are of my two companions who were worshipping Allah here with me. They died, I buried them here and erected a mosque between them, so that I could pray in it till such time when I join them." Then he reminisced the old days with them and talked of what they did. Then he wept and said:

"Rise, O my two friends, You have indeed slept for long. I find that you have still not finished your slumber. Do you not know that I am alone at Sam’aan? and I do not have anyone who I loved except you two? I shall stand by your graves, not departing, the whole night long, till I hear your voices, I shall weep over you as long as I live, and who is there to answer to one who laments, weeping? As if you two and death are the two sole objectives for my soul in my grave, the same way as it came upon you. And if a soul could act as a shield for another soul, I would have offered my soul to be your ransom."
